entities.summary:
The sixth cholera pandemic was a globally devastating disease outbreak spanning 1899 to 1923. It was the sixth major cholera pandemic in recorded history, with the first one occurring in 1775. Despite efforts to eradicate the disease, cholera would continue to plague the world for centuries. 

 This pandemic originated in the Indian subcontinent and spread rapidly to neighboring countries, eventually reaching as far as the Americas. Millions of people died as a result of the disease, making it one of the deadliest pandemics in human history. The pandemic also led to significant changes in public health infrastructure and policy, as well as the development of new treatments and vaccines. 

 One of the most significant consequences of the sixth cholera pandemic was the establishment of the Rockefeller Foundation's International Health Board in 1921, which aimed to combat infectious diseases around the world. The pandemic also led to increased investment in sanitation and water treatment infrastructure, particularly in urban areas. 

 'We must look to the source of the disease and try to understand what is causing it.' - Dr. Frederick Gates, one of the founders of the Rockefeller Foundation, in 1920.
